2.1.description: DUV and EUV exposure systems plus subsystem chain: light sources, optics, masks/pellicles, stages, overlay/alignment, and high-NA evolution. Most concentrated, capex-intensive chokepoint at advanced nodes.
2.1.name: Lithography equipment

2.2.description: CVD/ALD/PVD, plasma etch, implantation, RTP/anneal, CMP tools, epitaxy, furnaces. Creates and patterns every device layer; cycles with node transitions and capacity adds.
2.2.name: Deposition, etch, and process equipment

2.3.description: Wafer probe/sort, package test, burn-in, AOI, e-beam/optical inspection, CD/overlay metrology, defect inspection, film composition, electrical characterization. Tracks volume and yield-learning velocity.
2.3.name: Test, metrology, and inspection equipment

3.1.description: Architectures for matrix-heavy workloads: discrete GPUs, custom training/inference ASICs, FPGA acceleration, wafer-scale approaches. Primary driver of leading-edge wafers and advanced packaging.
3.1.name: AI accelerator and GPU design

3.3.description: DRAM for system memory, HBM for accelerator bandwidth, NAND for storage. HBM stacking and packaging complexity often binds accelerator supply.
3.3.name: Memory — DRAM, HBM, and NAND flash

3.5.description: 2.5D/3D integration, interposers, chip-on-wafer-on-substrate, fan-out WLP, bumping, pillars, underfill/molding, final test/burn-in. Packaging capacity increasingly binds accelerator supply and yield.
3.5.name: OSAT, advanced packaging, and assembly

4.2.description: High-layer server PCBs, HDI, flexible/rigid-flex, organic build-up substrates (ABF), emerging glass substrates. Substrate capacity can bind advanced packaging volumes.
4.2.layer_name: Passive Components, Substrates & Board-Level Supply Chain
4.2.name: Printed circuit boards and advanced packaging substrates

4.3.description: Underfills, mold compounds, solder balls/microbumps, copper pillars, TIMs, die-attach, encapsulants, epoxies. Qualification-locked materials constrain ramp speed and yield.
4.3.layer_name: Passive Components, Substrates & Board-Level Supply Chain
4.3.name: Packaging and thermal interface materials

5.1.description: System architecture/integration: boards, accelerator modules, interconnect topology, cooling integration, PSU specification, firmware/BMC, rack-scale design. Converts components into deployable compute.
5.1.name: Server and compute platform design

6.1.description: Develop/own/operate facilities: powered shells, leased capacity, wholesale/retail colocation, purpose-built AI campuses, edge operators. Real estate + operations layer consuming power, cooling, and connectivity at scale.
6.1.name: Datacenter operators and colocation providers

9.3.description: GPU/accelerator instances, dedicated GPU clouds, HPC-as-a-service, sovereign clouds. Aggregates infrastructure demand and sets compute pricing.
